clue.text: Order, say, two lots of aluminium with cheap bit thrown in

definitions.note: an adjective clued by an example of its use: alphabetical order is one kind of order

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are put in between the two copies of the metal symbol
two lots asks for the symbol for this metal to be written twice in a row

parts.note: Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

indicators.note: the words cheap bit are thrown about, so their letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An instruction to order two batches of aluminium with a cheap extra piece tossed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a verb or noun, but the definition describes a kind of order. 'thrown' makes PHABETIC; 'in' signals the insertion, 'two lots of' the doubling.
explanation.definitionFit: Alphabetical describes a sequence by letters, the commonest example of an ordering scheme.

clue.text: A chum married Nimby, for one

parts.note: a crony is a close chum

explanation.surface: A friend has married someone who objects to building near their home.
explanation.walkthrough: NIMBY stands for 'Not In My Back Yard', a word formed from initials; it is also a person, which is the misleading reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimby is formed from the initial letters of a phrase, making it an example of that kind of word.

clue.text: Issue one pound raised in merchandise

indicators.note: the reversed letters are placed in the middle of the verb for selling

parts.note: to merchandise goods is to push them, promote them for sale

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight

explanation.surface: A single pound coin goes up within the stock of goods being sold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'merchandise' is a verb here, to promote for sale. 'raised' reverses upwards in this down clue, giving BLI; 'in' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue a book or magazine is to put it out to the public, which is what a publisher does.

clue.text: Dimwit previously stole 'A New Feature of Poetry'

parts.note: an ass is a fool or dimwit

indicators.note: the adverb for formerly has stolen, taken in, the article and the letter for new

parts.note: once means at a previous time

explanation.surface: A fool earlier plagiarised a piece titled 'A New Feature of Poetry'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stole' looks like a past-tense theft or a scarf, but signals that ONCE takes in A and N: ON(AN)CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Assonance, the echoing of vowel sounds in nearby words, is a device used by poets.

clue.text: Turn out to be the last to join in eastern party

indicators.note: the picked letter goes in between the compass letter and the party

parts.note: the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

indicators.note: the last to points at the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone proves to be the final person to sign up to a party in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is a Northern Ireland political party; the last letter of 'join' goes in E + DUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To end up something is to finish by becoming it, the same as turning out to be it.

clue.text: Remote city in ruins rebuilt

indicators.note: the city abbreviation goes in the rearranged letters
rebuilt means the word ruins is put together in a new order

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, is the usual crossword city

explanation.surface: A distant city lying in ruins has been reconstructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ruins' looks like one phrase, but 'in' is the insertion signal; 'rebuilt' makes INSUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Insular means cut off like an island, so isolated and remote from others.

clue.text: African leader is circling a long time, twirling his weapon

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter
twirling turns the combination round so it reads backwards
the two letters of is circle, go round, the word for a long time

parts.note: ages means a long time

explanation.surface: An African chief has been spinning his spear for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes the first letter; 'circling' gives IAGESS and 'twirling' reverses it to SSEGAI.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender spear used by peoples of southern Africa, so the African's weapon.

clue.text: English team in large firm chart last of May and Johnson's work

indicators.note: the team letters sit inside the letters for large firm

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team
a graph is a chart

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An English side inside a big company plots the end of May and Johnson's activity.
explanation.walkthrough: XI is eleven, a cricket or football team. 'last of' takes Y from May. 'May and Johnson' suggests two politicians; the Johnson meant is Samuel Johnson.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Johnson compiled his famous Dictionary of 1755, so compiling dictionaries was his work.

clue.text: Carried by sea westwards, third of team's missing coats

indicators.note: missing means that letter is taken out
in an across clue, westwards means reading right to left, so backwards

parts.note: seaborne means carried by sea

indicators.note: third of picks the third letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Something carried west by sea has lost the third of a team's coats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'westwards' reverses SEABORNE to ENROBAES; 'missing' takes out A, the third letter of 'team's'.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrobe is to dress or cover, as a confectioner covers sweets in chocolate.

clue.text: Abandoned South American stopped ringing

indicators.note: ringing means surrounding, so the word for stopped forms a ring round the other letters

parts.note: an engine that died stopped

explanation.surface: An abandoned South American bell has ceased chiming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' sounds like bells, but it is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Disused means no longer used, so left abandoned, like a derelict railway line.

clue.text: Some stars support speech, the result of 7

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting part sits below the other, so the speech word comes first

parts.note: diction is a manner of speech
Aries is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: Certain celebrities endorse a speech that results from something.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' is the answer to 7 Down, LEXICOGRAPHY, the craft of compiling the words in these books.
explanation.definitionFit: Lexicography is the compiling of reference books of words, and those books are its product.

clue.text: Trendy soldier's over visiting, notes swinger outside bar

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy

indicators.note: the reversed letters visit, go inside, the two letters for notes

parts.note: N is an abbreviation for note, so two notes give two Ns

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: GI is an American soldier; GI's gives GIS

explanation.surface: A fashionable soldier's visit is over, and music plays near a person swinging outside a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses, 'visiting' inserts. The 'swinger' is the sign hanging outside a pub, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub's painted sign hangs from a bracket outside and swings in the wind.

clue.text: When swimming, plaice swallow gallons of ocean

indicators.note: the rearranged letters swallow, take inside, the letter for gallons
swimming suggests the letters of plaice are moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: Swimming fish take in gallons of seawater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' turns PLAICE into PELAIC, and 'swallow' puts G inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelagic means relating to the open sea, as with fish that live far from the shore.

clue.text: Work hard to acquire some essentially sexy allure

indicators.note: the letters for work and hard acquire, take inside, the picked letters

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: essentially means the essence, the inner letters, of the next word

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Putting in hard work to gain a bit of sex appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes the inner letters of 'some', and 'to acquire' signals the insertion; 'sexy' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is informal for vigour or glamour, especially physical attractiveness.

clue.text: Queen once has European hat back to front in part of UK

indicators.note: these letters go in between the letters for the region

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, part of the United Kingdom

indicators.note: back to front means the end of the word is moved round to the front

parts.note: titfer is rhyming slang for hat (tit for tat)

explanation.surface: A former queen wears a European hat the wrong way round in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: TITFER is British rhyming slang for hat; 'back to front' moves its back half, FER, to the front: FERTIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefertiti was a queen of ancient Egypt, wife of the pharaoh Akhenaten.

clue.text: American wears fake top and army headgear

indicators.note: the word for fake wears, has on its body, the letter for American

parts.note: to forge is to fake
a cap is a top, as on a bottle

explanation.surface: A US soldier sports a counterfeit shirt and military hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wears' puts A into FORGE: FOR(A)GE.
explanation.definitionFit: A forage cap is a soft peaked military cap worn by soldiers off parade.

clue.text: Storyteller regularly read books in heart of Paris

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the next word
the books abbreviation goes in the French word

parts.note: coeur is French for heart, the word used in Paris
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: Someone who reads books often in central Paris tells stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' gives RA; 'heart of Paris' looks like the middle letter of PARIS but is COEUR, French for heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a person skilled at telling anecdotes in an entertaining way.

clue.text: Series covering last British king's mortification

indicators.note: the series word covers, surrounds, the king's letters

parts.note: a chain is a series of linked things
George VI was the last British king; GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: A sequence of events covering the last king's embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: George VI was the last British king; his royal cipher, Georgius Rex, appears on postboxes. 'covering' signals the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is annoyance and distress at being humiliated, closely matching mortification.

clue.text: Workers collect delicious drink from this battered crate in city

definitions.text: Workers collect delicious drink from this

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go in the city abbreviation

parts.note: NY is New York

indicators.note: battered means the word crate is knocked out of shape, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Labourers take a tasty drink from a beaten-up crate in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Workers' are worker bees, not labourers, and the drink is nectar; 'battered' turns CRATE into ECTAR, put in NY.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectary is the gland in a flower that secretes the nectar bees gather.

clue.text: Children hand in tin

indicators.note: the hand word goes in the symbol for the metal

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
a paw is jocularly a hand

explanation.surface: Children put a hand inside a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Spawn is used, often disparagingly, for offspring, a person's children.

clue.text: Flier, black one, blocks main road

indicators.note: the two letters block, sit in the way between, the words for main and road

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A black flying object blocks the main road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main road' reads as one phrase, but splits in two, and 'blocks' puts the black one between the halves.
explanation.definitionFit: A seabird such as a gull or gannet is a bird, which is a flier.

clue.text: Motorists in Malta spoiled former capital

indicators.note: the motoring letters go in the rearranged letters
spoiled means the word Malta is damaged, its letters rearranged

parts.note: the AA, Automobile Association, is a British motorists' organisation

explanation.surface: Drivers in Malta have wrecked a one-time capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The Automobile Association is a British motoring club. 'spoiled' makes ALMTA and 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Alma-Ata, now Almaty, was the capital of Kazakhstan until Astana replaced it in 1997.

clue.text: Our neighbour's front replaced with first of painted struts

indicators.note: the opening letter of the country's name is swapped for another letter

parts.note: France is Britain's neighbour, so our neighbour's is France's

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: The front of a neighbouring country's building is fitted with painted supports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struts' reads as the noun for supports but is a verb here: walks proudly.
explanation.definitionFit: To prance is to walk with exaggerated, showy steps, which is to strut.

clue.text: Period working out in southern lakes

indicators.note: the exercise letters go in between the others

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake, so LL for lakes
PE, physical education, is working out

explanation.surface: Time spent exercising in the lakes of the south.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell is a period of time, as in a spell of fine weather.

clue.text: A short distance divides Greek and Arab school

indicators.note: the inserted letters divide, sit between, the two abbreviations

parts.note: AR is the abbreviation for Arab or Arabic
mm, a millimetre, is a short distance

explanation.surface: A small gap separates Greek and Arab pupils at a school.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a grammar school is a selective state secondary school.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar is short for grammar school, a type of academically selective secondary school.

clue.text: Distance covered reversing, say, a cart

indicators.note: reversing turns the whole string round to read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means here
a dray is a low cart for heavy loads

explanation.surface: Distance travelled while backing up a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' applies to EG + A + DRAY together.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardage is a distance measured in yards, as gained by a player in American football.

clue.text: Pen round old popular invention

indicators.note: the word for pen goes round the other letters

parts.note: a pen for animals is a cage
in means popular

explanation.surface: A pen surrounding an old and popular invention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' suggests writing, but is an enclosure here.
explanation.definitionFit: A coinage is a newly invented word or phrase.

clue.text: Cynic with dope and ale disrupted source of dope

indicators.note: disrupted says the words are broken up and their letters put in a new order

explanation.surface: A cynic with drugs and beer is the disruptive origin of narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' appears twice: once as letters in the anagram, then in its slang sense of information.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for information, and an encyclopedia is a reference source of facts.
